chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The pigeon is a bird from the birds of the Prophets (peace be upon them) which they used to keep in their houses, and there is no house in which there is a pigeon except that no affliction from the jinn would befall the inhabitants of that house. The foolish ones among the jinn tamper in the house, so they tamper with the pigeons and leave the people alone.'
He (the narrator) said: 'So I saw in the rooms of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a pigeon for his son Ismail.'

key_terms.آفة: affliction/blight — harm, plague, or misfortune, particularly that caused by spiritual forces
key_terms.الحمام: pigeon/dove — the bird referenced throughout, kept for prophetic tradition and spiritual protection
key_terms.سفهاء الجن: foolish ones of the jinn — the mischievous, reckless segment of the jinn who cause household disturbances
key_terms.طيور الأنبياء: birds of the Prophets — indicating prophetic practice and recommendation

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophets keep pigeons in their homes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the pigeon as a bird traditionally kept by the Prophets in their homes, and explains that its presence in a house protects the inhabitants from harm by mischievous jinn. The jinn, being distracted by the pigeon, leave the human residents undisturbed. This teaching reflects a broader Shia understanding of the natural world as imbued with spiritual significance, where certain elements — like the pigeon — serve protective and blessed functions. The narrator corroborates this by noting that Imam al-Sadiq himself kept pigeons in his home for his son Ismail.
